reason: While Yahweh is unquestionably depicted as all-powerful through the miraculous plagues (blood, frogs, gnats, flies, livestock disease, hail, locusts) and explicit declarations ('אֵין כָּמֹנִי בְּכָל־ הָאָֽרֶץ' - 'There is none like me in all the earth'), the characterization as 'remote' does not apply. The text shows Yahweh in constant, direct communication with Moses. God speaks to Moses repeatedly, responds immediately to Moses's prayers and cries ('וַיִּצְעַק מֹשֶׁה אֶל־ יְהוָה'), and is intimately involved in guiding events moment-by-moment. The relationship is relational and engaged rather than distant or remote. God works through intermediaries (Moses and Aaron), but this reflects delegation, not detachment. The depiction is of an active, responsive God deeply invested in the liberation of Israel.
